To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

GAN-assisted Model Compression (GAN-MC), which augments the compression dataset with data from a GAN trained to approximate the teacher model's training distribution, significantly improves model compression performance for deep neural networks and random forests, and a metric we propose, the Compression Score, which evaluates the quality of a synthetic dataset based on the performance of models compressed with it, is a better measure of the usefulness of a GAN for model compression than the popular Inception metric.

GAN-assisted Model Compression significantly improves student accuracy and we propose the Compression Score to evaluate the quality of a synthetic data set based on its induced model compression performance, and we show that the Compression Score captures both discriminability and diversity and is a better evaluation metric than Inception Score.

GANs can help improve student model accuracy during model compression, and a metric that captures both data diversity & discriminability is useful for assessing synthetic datasets in model compression.
